Thank you Cydney Hayes and Gazetteer SF for the thoughtful profile of Studio BBA, "It's Studio BBA's city, we just live in it."

Cydney spent time with us in the Studio, and the piece traces our work from Flora Grubb Gardens through the cafes, restaurants, homes, and offices we've designed across San Francisco and the Bay Area since Bonnie opened the doors in 1992.

What we hope comes through is what drives all of it: designing spaces that let people be people, with daylight, good acoustics, natural materials, and room to connect. That work only happens because of the clients who trust us, the craftspeople who build what we draw, and our small team that cares about every detail.

Thank you to everyone who's been a part of it. Read the full article at link in bio.

It's been a joy to work with Tartine again, and we're proud to share their newest location, just across the Bridge in Mill Valley.

The design starts with a quiet flour-white and wood-on-wood palette. The red oak millwork features tile accents that add a pop of color and a durable finish that stands up to daily wear and cleaning. Custom steel painted in an oxide red accents the retail displays, baking area, and light fixture brackets, keeping the space feeling rooted in Marin rather than borrowed from France. Tartine is of Mill Valley, and we wanted the space to reflect that.

The community's response has been remarkable. There have been lines out the door since the soft opening, and they haven't let up. 

Looking forward to sharing more about the Downtown San Francisco @TartineBakery we're currently working on.

We're not here to greenwash—we're here to design spaces that last.

For us, sustainability isn't about chasing certifications or buzzwords. It's about making choices that respect materials, reduce waste, and create spaces people don't want to replace. That means adaptive reuse and renovations over demolition. Durable finishes over trendy ones. Quality pieces that can move with you, grow with you, and be repaired when needed.

We also believe plants and landscape aren't just aesthetic—they're essential to the human experience. Natural light, borrowed views, greenery, and fresh air aren't luxuries. They're what make a space feel good to inhabit.

The most sustainable choice is often the simplest: keep things out of the landfill. Buy once, buy well. Repair instead of replace. Design for longevity, not obsolescence.

Cheap materials don't save money when you're replacing and repairing constantly—they just fill landfills and create more work down the line. We'd rather invest in something that lasts.

Happy Earth Day. Here's to building better, not just more. 🌱

Sometimes my nose is so deep in my work, that I forget this might be your first time choosing an architect or designer. At Studio BBA, we think holistically about design and how that impacts and elevates the human experience. For us, that means considering acoustics, natural day lighting, task / ambient / and decorative lighting, finishes, and scale but also furnishings, accessories and plants.

We prepare space plans and permits for your new interconnecting stair and custom bike storage. Beyond traditional architecture, we also provide interior architecture and design through finish and furniture selections. But we don't stop there, we design your plant program, select accessories and facilitate custom art and signage.

A project in progress — and one we've loved every step of the way.

The West Sonoma ADU is a compact, light-filled home tucked into the oak woodland of Sebastopol, designed for a wonderful couple settling into a new chapter closer to family. At under 1,200 square feet, the home is sized to what matters: south-facing views of the Sonoma hills, warm wood interiors, and a seamless connection to the landscape outside.
Working with clients who bring this much thoughtfulness and warmth to the process is exactly why we do this work.

Great hospitality design is about creating spaces that feel alive—buzzing with energy, conversation, and the kind of magic that only happens when people gather.

For this project, we leaned into the sensory experience: warm, layered materials, lighting that shifts from day to night, and a layout that encourages lingering. We wanted guests to feel the craft and intention in every detail, from the custom millwork to the way natural light moves through the space.

The design celebrates San Francisco's historic Chinatown, drawing inspiration from Hong Kong alleyways and Chinese culinary traditions, while creating something entirely its own. It's a place that honors its roots while feeling fresh and alive.

Since opening, it's become exactly what we hoped—a space where the community gathers, celebrates, and keeps coming back.

Sometimes the best way forward is to step away from the screen. When we’re searching for inspiration or feeling stuck, we reach for trace paper, pencils, and markers — and just draw. There’s something about the tactile process of sketching that unlocks a different kind of thinking. In an increasingly digital world, we’re proud to keep the analog alive.

Reminiscing right along with @MisterJius as they celebrate 10 years since opening, and since we completed their space. These vintage light fixtures are such a strong part of the identity, we wanted to share some site photos of the salvaged chandeliers and some of the exploration we did to dim and diffuse the lamps.

Also, swipe to the end for this obligatory share - Bonnie and @BrandoJ with 🚨 plucked ducks 🚨 leading up to the grand opening of Mister Jius in Chinatown.

Downsizing square footage doesn't mean compromising on experience—it means being smarter about every inch.

This office renovation focused on quality over quantity, investing in design that feels intentional and welcoming. We created a layout that prevents small teams from feeling lost on a larger floor plate, using furniture, materiality, and thoughtful spatial planning to define intimate zones within the open plan.

Every detail—from the acoustic drapery to the custom millwork—serves both a functional and atmospheric purpose. The goal was a space that works as well for daily grinding as it does for all-hands meetings and hosting clients.

Our clients tell us their team actually looks forward to coming in. That's how we measure success.

Here's a round up of our favorite green moments from Studio BBA projects. 🍀

The best offices don't feel like offices at all—they feel like places people actually want to be.

For this workplace project, we focused on creating distinct zones that support different ways of working, from focused individual tasks to collaborative team sessions. The challenge was designing for flexibility in a post-pandemic world where teams are smaller but the need for connection is bigger than ever.

Thoughtful acoustic treatments, varied seating options, and strategic access to natural light help the space feel both energizing and calm. We worked closely with our client to understand how their team actually works, then designed around those rhythms rather than imposing a one-size-fits-all solution.

The result is a space that adapts to the people in it, not the other way around.

This home is a study in restraint and refinement—honoring its 1940's ranch roots while serving the modern life of its owners.

We focused on a few key interventions that would have the biggest impact. The great room and outdoor living spaces became the heart of the renovation, with reclaimed douglas fir and aged white oak creating a calm, timeless palette.

The design philosophy was simple: respect the bones of the house, invest in craft and quality where it matters, and let the architecture breathe. Small, well-executed details— exposed douglas fir beams, hand-hewn wood floors, and multi-slide pocket door—add up to a home that feels both fresh and grounded in its history.

Our clients have lived here for nearly a decade, and seeing how they've made the space their own reminds us why we love this work.
